items.statement: Start discovery by understanding likely users, what they are trying to do, how they do it now, frustrations and needs.
items.limitations: Apply only within stated scope; inspect source and project constraints for material decisions.

items.statement: Define success in terms of metrics that indicate whether the service is solving the intended problem, and combine performance data with user research.
items.limitations: Apply only within stated scope; inspect source and project constraints for material decisions.

items.statement: Discovery should examine value, usability, feasibility and viability risk, but their materiality varies by initiative.
items.limitations: Apply only within stated scope; inspect source and project constraints for material decisions.

items.statement: An opportunity-solution tree can connect a desired outcome to opportunities, candidate solutions and assumption tests.
items.limitations: Apply only within stated scope; inspect source and project constraints for material decisions.

items.statement: Quality attributes should be elicited from stakeholder/business goals before architecture choices are fixed.
items.limitations: Apply only within stated scope; inspect source and project constraints for material decisions.

items.statement: Architecture documentation should capture goals, constraints, context, runtime/deployment views, important decisions, quality requirements and risks at useful detail.
items.limitations: Apply only within stated scope; inspect source and project constraints for material decisions.

items.statement: Architecture diagrams should use audience-appropriate levels of abstraction; system context and container views are often sufficient.
items.limitations: Apply only within stated scope; inspect source and project constraints for material decisions.

items.statement: Secure development practices must be integrated through the SDLC rather than added only at the end.
items.limitations: Apply only within stated scope; inspect source and project constraints for material decisions.

items.statement: Security maturity spans governance, design, implementation, verification and operations.
items.limitations: Apply only within stated scope; inspect source and project constraints for material decisions.

items.statement: OpenAPI provides a formal description of an HTTP API surface and semantics; API contracts should be machine-readable where useful.
items.limitations: Apply only within stated scope; inspect source and project constraints for material decisions.

items.statement: HTTP API errors can use standardized machine-readable problem details instead of inventing incompatible error envelopes.
items.limitations: Apply only within stated scope; inspect source and project constraints for material decisions.

items.statement: SLOs should be explicit reliability targets tied to user-facing indicators and used for prioritization, not just reporting.
items.limitations: Apply only within stated scope; inspect source and project constraints for material decisions.

items.statement: Delivery performance should be measured with throughput and instability metrics over time and interpreted in system context.
items.limitations: Apply only within stated scope; inspect source and project constraints for material decisions.

items.statement: Accessibility is an end-to-end quality property requiring semantics, keyboard/focus behavior and manual validation proportional to risk.
items.limitations: Apply only within stated scope; inspect source and project constraints for material decisions.

items.statement: Domain models should distinguish evidence/facts from hypotheses and challenge boundaries before implementation architecture.
items.limitations: Apply only within stated scope; inspect source and project constraints for material decisions.

items.statement: Use explicit product quality characteristics and quality scenarios to drive architecture trade-offs rather than selecting patterns by preference.
items.limitations: Apply only within stated scope; inspect project constraints and failure modes for material decisions.

items.statement: Architecture documentation should separate context, building blocks, runtime, deployment, quality requirements, risks and significant decisions so different concerns remain inspectable.
items.limitations: Apply only within stated scope; inspect project constraints and failure modes for material decisions.

items.statement: HTTP method semantics include safety and idempotency properties; retries must respect method/application semantics rather than assuming every request is retry-safe.
items.limitations: Apply only within stated scope; inspect project constraints and failure modes for material decisions.

items.statement: A database update plus external message publish is a dual-write consistency problem; transactional outbox is one valid pattern when those effects must be coordinated.
items.limitations: Apply only within stated scope; inspect project constraints and failure modes for material decisions.

items.statement: At-least-once delivery can produce duplicate processing; consumers or effect handlers need explicit idempotency where duplicate effects are harmful.
items.limitations: Apply only within stated scope; inspect project constraints and failure modes for material decisions.

items.statement: Avoid redundant, contradictory and duplicated UI state; derive values when possible and keep state ownership explicit.
items.limitations: Apply only within stated scope; inspect project constraints and failure modes for material decisions.

items.statement: Effects are for synchronization with external systems; avoid using them as a default mechanism for ordinary derived state or user-event logic.
items.limitations: Apply only within stated scope; inspect project constraints and failure modes for material decisions.

items.statement: Persistence design must make transactional consistency, isolation, locking and concurrency assumptions explicit for critical mutations.
items.limitations: Apply only within stated scope; inspect project constraints and failure modes for material decisions.

items.statement: Schema migrations are production changes with compatibility and recovery implications; applied migrations should be immutable and later changes expressed as new migrations.
items.limitations: Apply only within stated scope; inspect project constraints and failure modes for material decisions.

items.statement: Performance should be expressed through user-relevant response measures and budgets, then verified with workload-appropriate evidence rather than averages alone.
items.limitations: Apply only within stated scope; inspect project constraints and failure modes for material decisions.

items.statement: Testing strategy should be driven by product/system risks and guarantees, choosing the lowest layer that can honestly prove each property.
items.limitations: Apply proportional to risk and workload; tooling evidence does not replace domain-specific validation.

items.statement: Automated browser tests are appropriate for critical integrated user flows, but should not replace lower-layer invariant/contract tests.
items.limitations: Apply proportional to risk and workload; tooling evidence does not replace domain-specific validation.

items.statement: Accessibility automation detects a subset of issues; manual keyboard/assistive-technology verification remains necessary for critical flows.
items.limitations: Apply proportional to risk and workload; tooling evidence does not replace domain-specific validation.

items.statement: Threat modeling is a structured, repeatable design-time process and should be revisited as the system changes.
items.limitations: Apply proportional to risk and workload; tooling evidence does not replace domain-specific validation.

items.statement: Security requirements, risks and design decisions should be tracked through the SDLC.
items.limitations: Apply proportional to risk and workload; tooling evidence does not replace domain-specific validation.

items.statement: Software release provenance provides verifiable information about where, when and how an artifact was produced.
items.limitations: Apply proportional to risk and workload; tooling evidence does not replace domain-specific validation.

items.statement: Open-source dependency posture can be assessed with automated supply-chain signals, but such scores are input evidence rather than a complete security verdict.
items.limitations: Apply proportional to risk and workload; tooling evidence does not replace domain-specific validation.

items.statement: Performance goals should be stated as explicit budgets/limits rather than assumed to emerge from good implementation.
items.limitations: Apply proportional to risk and workload; tooling evidence does not replace domain-specific validation.

items.statement: Baseline, stress, spike and soak tests answer different performance/reliability questions and require workload models that match the risk.
items.limitations: Apply proportional to risk and workload; tooling evidence does not replace domain-specific validation.

items.statement: Performance test pass/fail criteria should include latency percentiles, throughput/error behavior and correctness under load, not average latency alone.
items.limitations: Apply proportional to risk and workload; tooling evidence does not replace domain-specific validation.

items.statement: Release automation reduces manual inconsistency and improves knowledge of rollout state; partial/canary rollout can evaluate a change before full exposure.
items.limitations: Adapt to service criticality, deployment platform and operational ownership.

items.statement: A release should be traceable to an exact source/build artifact, with deployment evidence preserved rather than inferred from branch state.
items.limitations: Adapt to service criticality, deployment platform and operational ownership.

items.statement: Observability should combine signals such as traces, metrics and logs with shared context rather than rely on a single undifferentiated log stream.
items.limitations: Adapt to service criticality, deployment platform and operational ownership.

items.statement: Tracing represents the path of a request through a system and is useful for cross-component latency/failure diagnosis.
items.limitations: Adapt to service criticality, deployment platform and operational ownership.

items.statement: Reliability objectives should be expressed through SLOs and used to make prioritization decisions, not merely displayed as dashboards.
items.limitations: Adapt to service criticality, deployment platform and operational ownership.

items.statement: Alerts should be actionable and tied to user-impacting reliability objectives where practical; noisy non-actionable alerts create operational toil.
items.limitations: Adapt to service criticality, deployment platform and operational ownership.

items.statement: Postmortems should turn incidents into system/process learning and tracked follow-up rather than blame or undocumented memory.
items.limitations: Adapt to service criticality, deployment platform and operational ownership.

items.statement: Backup configuration is not recovery evidence; restore procedures must be exercised and measured against recovery objectives.
items.limitations: Adapt to service criticality, deployment platform and operational ownership.

items.statement: Delivery performance should be measured over time using throughput and instability indicators in the context of a specific service/application.
items.limitations: Adapt to service criticality, deployment platform and operational ownership.

items.statement: A production rollout is not complete at deployment: health, smoke, telemetry and rollback/forward-fix readiness need explicit evidence.
items.limitations: Adapt to service criticality, deployment platform and operational ownership.

items.statement: Metrics should start from product/service purpose and goals, then map to observable signals and measures rather than starting from available events.
items.limitations: Metric/experiment interpretation depends on product context, data quality and population; avoid universal thresholds.

items.statement: User-centered product measurement can combine dimensions such as happiness, engagement, adoption, retention and task success; not every dimension is relevant to every product.
items.limitations: Metric/experiment interpretation depends on product context, data quality and population; avoid universal thresholds.

items.statement: Performance metrics should be combined with user research and other data sources; digital analytics alone is insufficient to explain user problems.
items.limitations: Metric/experiment interpretation depends on product context, data quality and population; avoid universal thresholds.

items.statement: A North Star metric is useful only when it reflects user value and is connected to controllable product inputs; it is a supporting framework, not a universal requirement.
items.limitations: Metric/experiment interpretation depends on product context, data quality and population; avoid universal thresholds.

items.statement: Randomized controlled experiments can establish causal effects of product changes when randomization, instrumentation and analysis assumptions are valid.
items.limitations: Metric/experiment interpretation depends on product context, data quality and population; avoid universal thresholds.

items.statement: A/B testing is one evidence method among others; it requires sufficient traffic, a causal question and trustworthy assignment/measurement.
items.limitations: Metric/experiment interpretation depends on product context, data quality and population; avoid universal thresholds.

items.statement: Sample Ratio Mismatch is a trustworthiness warning; experiment conclusions should not be used until the mismatch is diagnosed/resolved.
items.limitations: Metric/experiment interpretation depends on product context, data quality and population; avoid universal thresholds.

items.statement: Feature flags separate exposure from deployment, but experiments still require explicit hypothesis, population, metrics, guardrails and lifecycle/cleanup.
items.limitations: Metric/experiment interpretation depends on product context, data quality and population; avoid universal thresholds.

items.statement: Production performance data should be used to identify improvement opportunities and paired with research to understand why behavior occurs.
items.limitations: Metric/experiment interpretation depends on product context, data quality and population; avoid universal thresholds.

items.statement: Continuous discovery should connect desired outcomes to observed opportunities, solutions and assumption tests so learning feeds the next decision.
items.limitations: Metric/experiment interpretation depends on product context, data quality and population; avoid universal thresholds.

items.statement: When domain boundaries are uncertain, compare alternative decompositions and challenge them using language, invariants, temporal rules, ownership, change coupling and autonomy before fixing architecture.
items.limitations: Project context and stronger scoped evidence may override this default through an explicit decision record.

items.statement: Tactical aggregates and implementation patterns should follow sufficiently justified strategic boundaries; database tables and screen nouns are not aggregate/context definitions by default.
items.limitations: Project context and stronger scoped evidence may override this default through an explicit decision record.

items.statement: Material requirements should preserve traceability from evidence/outcome through scenario and acceptance criteria to verification, while hypotheses remain labeled as hypotheses.
items.limitations: Project context and stronger scoped evidence may override this default through an explicit decision record.

items.statement: UI architecture decisions should begin with context of use, hard constraints and task requirements before selecting patterns or component libraries.
items.limitations: Project context and stronger scoped evidence may override this default through an explicit decision record.

items.statement: Consequential workflows need explicit loading/empty/error/stale/pending/conflict/recovery behavior and adaptive transformation, not only happy-path screens.
items.limitations: Project context and stronger scoped evidence may override this default through an explicit decision record.

items.statement: Choose implementation adapters after behavior and semantics are decided; component-library availability is not evidence that a pattern is correct.
items.limitations: Project context and stronger scoped evidence may override this default through an explicit decision record.

items.statement: Shared interaction patterns should move from Local to Extended/Core only when reuse, semantic stability, accessibility coverage, ownership and migration cost justify promotion.
items.limitations: Project context and stronger scoped evidence may override this default through an explicit decision record.

items.statement: Visual design should establish hierarchy and constrained scales for spacing/type/color/depth instead of making isolated decorative decisions per screen.
items.limitations: Project context and stronger scoped evidence may override this default through an explicit decision record.

items.statement: Empty states, readable widths, semantic color usage and information hierarchy are functional interface decisions, not finishing decoration.
items.limitations: Project context and stronger scoped evidence may override this default through an explicit decision record.

items.statement: Reusable knowledge needs provenance, scope, verification date, lifecycle and explicit supersession so new guidance does not silently erase older decisions.
items.limitations: Project context and stronger scoped evidence may override this default through an explicit decision record.

items.statement: Material decisions should record evidence, considered options, trade-offs, validation and observable revisit triggers so they can be reviewed and superseded deliberately.
items.limitations: Project context and stronger scoped evidence may override this default through an explicit decision record.

items.statement: AI-assisted delivery quality depends on the surrounding harness: explicit context, tool and capability constraints, quality gates, observability and security controls; model capability alone is not sufficient evidence of safe delivery.
items.limitations: Practitioner reports and operational observations support the direction; project-specific controls still require local threat/risk analysis and verification.

items.statement: Production telemetry, user feedback and operational evidence should feed back into product and engineering decisions rather than treating deployment as the terminal lifecycle state.
items.scope: production learning and outcome-driven software lifecycle
items.limitations: The report frames the lifecycle and Definition of Value; concrete learning classification and propagation rules in this OS are a local design decision.

items.statement: Model selection, context reuse and tool-output volume can materially change AI operating cost; context/tool contracts are therefore engineering and cost controls, not only prompt concerns.
items.scope: coding-agent workloads comparable to the report's measured environment
items.limitations: Reported percentages are workload/model/provider specific and must not be generalized as universal savings.

items.statement: Project conventions can be discovered from multiple repository-local and review sources, deduplicated, conflict-checked and confidence-scored before a human promotes them to intended standards.
items.scope: project-specific standards discovery in AI-assisted development
items.limitations: Practitioner implementation evidence. Confidence in an observation does not grant authority; repository frequency may encode accidental legacy behavior.

items.statement: Task-local orchestration state and durable phase artifacts can support pause/resume and operator visibility across long AI-assisted workflows.
items.limitations: Task state is an orchestration aid, not stronger evidence than actual repository behavior, Git state or executable verification.
